beats: Hook: what if your tensor is mostly zeros (line_sparse_muffin_tray), or changes shape with every request (line_dyn_party_queue)?
The recipe so far: algorithm + schedule + tuner, one kitchen. Three awkward cases: many GPUs, mostly zeros, shapes that change.

Many GPUs, CoCoNet (ASPLOS 2022): communication goes into the language; data parallel (each kitchen cooks whole dishes for half the orders, line_multi_dp_plates) and tensor parallel (each kitchen makes half of every dish, line_multi_tp_halves) are two schedules of one program; overlap passing with cooking.

Mercury (SOSP 2025): lockstep collectives make everyone wait for the slowest (line_multi_wait_barrier); the 'shift' primitive starts each GPU on a different chunk and rotates, everyone busy on a different dish, then pass it on (line_multi_pass_dishes; line_whisper_line / line_round_table for ring vs all-at-once).
Mostly zeros, TACO: sparse formats and sparse loops, so you stop checking empty cups (line_sparse_muffin_tray).
Fractal (ASPLOS 2024): group the zeros into blocks the hardware likes (line_sparse_trays_grouped); 'perforate' skips whole rows of the loop (line_sparse_perforate).

Shapes that change, DietCode (MLSys 2022): one tuned kernel per shape does not scale (line_dyn_tin_shelf); tune small micro-kernels once and compose any size, a dispatcher picks the mix (line_dyn_push_tables).
Takeaway: same recipe, new primitives for each awkward case; the speaker's own favourites are Mercury and Fractal (check before saying).
